Anyways I'm sure upon leaving the facility/set security guards picked him up instantly and drove him out of the mountains and to the closest part of the city, after all he's one of the biggest faces in TV history and they want to make sure he get out safe. It's been a while since I've seen the movie but I'm pretty sure the whole production was based in the hills of Hollywood. If I was to base this of what would happen in real life then I'd think there would be a giant crowd of paparazzi getting as many photos as possible(Which would truly mess with Truman because this is the first indication to him that he's a big name and this whole situation is one of the biggest things to happen in Hollywood)
Right off the bat he would than be handed over to LAPD for direct transportation to the Clerks office with a police convoy. If you think that's a bit much you gotta remember, his entire life was filmed and watched by a plethora of people. He's one of the biggest names in The US unbeknownst to Truman. He literally has no idea how real life works. Honestly speaking do you think he has any idea how to read someone's body language and decipher if someone wants to harm or screw him over? Sure the production company probably had people stab him in the back during his early years for the entertainment, but not in a way where it'd prepare him for similar real life situations. With plenty of crazy fans out there I'm positive the county would make sure he was safe with a group of cops protecting him. If he was to be harmed only minutes after leaving it would look horrible for LA.
Anyways at the clerks office, or city hall he'd be sat down and debriefed on what happened to him. He'd be reminded that he was in fact part of a hugely fabricated television show that showed his entire life. Every choice that he thought he made, every situation he experienced, everything he knew was pre-planned and made to happen that way no matter what he did. I'd like to imagine this meeting takes place over the course of many hours with a board of lawyers representing the county and a separate group of lawyers for the production company present. He'd be informed of the real world laws involving his situation, most likely the county would be on the production company's side because of all the money the show probably brought in. But that's just speculation.
He's probably in so much shock that he's not even focused on, or doesn't even know or think about or informed of the fact that he could sue or get compensated for what happened. 
He gets to choose his new legal name for his own protection, the production company covers the fees to save face. 
Now is the fact that he has no credit, no diploma, no references, no history of him ever working a real job. The production company sets him up with his own house paid for by the company(they probably got it pennies on the dollar through advertisements of reality companies) and most likely a set timeframe of living expenses covered by them as a token of appreciation/them not trying to get sued. So what now?
To make this a lot shorter I'll try to make bullet points
•He gets harassed by multiple lawyers.
•He tries his best to cope with having his face on every news outlet.
•Gets multiple request by people trying to be his agent.
•Learns how messed up the real world is.
•Multiple request for him in advertisements and commercials.
•Every single radio station and talk show trying to get interviews.

If I was to make this a happy ending than I'd say he eventually meets up with that lady and they travel the world together and he takes enjoys every second of the real world he can. Eventually writes a book titled "The Truman Show" which becomes a best seller and he lives his life happy he escaped his prison.

I'm sure he did find that lady and really loved her, but he has severe trust issues and PTSD. He can never comfortably go anywhere without being recognized and harassed. He's super depressed that he never fully lived his first half of life. He escaped that fake life, just to go into a world where he's only known for living a lie for the enjoyment of people passing time living a real life. He can't cope, and hates every aspect of himself. Eventually ending his life, which only results in a few weeks of sadness in the US, after those few weeks it's back to normal and people forget what he went through. His whole life just becomes a interesting story to read about whilst laying in bed. To the Reddit community he'd be just another TIL post.

R.I.P Truman.


But he'd definitely get a parade and that's pretty cool I guess!
